title: Right-turn-on-red study and Cambridge ION engagement
subtitle: Also: Kitchener transit hub construction updates, George Street closure, Woolwich parking penalties, Highland Road noise, Cambridge annexation
overview: The Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee asked staff to study banning right turns on red at high-collision intersections on regional arterial roads, and to look at leading pedestrian intervals {{vote:m8}}. Staff will report back on feasibility, costs and a preliminary list of candidate intersections. Council would still have to consider any change.

The committee also recommended closing a non-travelled part of George Street North in Cambridge {{vote:m4}}, and directed staff to report by the end of 2025 on how the Region will keep residents and businesses informed about Kitchener Central Transit Hub and GO Expansion construction {{vote:m5}}. A consent agenda also backed a minor boundary change between Cambridge and North Dumfries and administrative parking penalties on regional roads in Woolwich {{vote:m1}}.

Committee received a report on Stage 2 ION engagement for information. An initial business case is expected in November 2025. It also received a report on Highland Road noise, where staff did not recommend a noise wall. Several delegates spoke in favour of extending ION light rail into Cambridge. Council would still have to adopt the committee's recommendations.

decisions.item: Right turn on red and pedestrian signals study
decisions.detail: The committee asked staff to report on prohibiting right turns on red and introducing leading pedestrian intervals at high-collision regional intersections, including a preliminary list of candidate intersections {{vote:m8}}.
The committee recommended permanently closing a non-travelled part of Regional Road 42 (George Street North) and removing it from the Regional Road System {{vote:m4}}.

The committee directed staff to report back by the end of Q4 2025 on community updates and engagement with residents, businesses and the BIA on hub and GO Expansion construction, with Metrolinx asked to take part {{vote:m5}}.
The committee recommended that the Region support the minor restructuring proposal for Cambridge to annex certain lands from North Dumfries, as described in report PDL-GDS-25-011.
The committee recommended amending the Traffic and Parking By-law to allow administrative penalties for parking on regional roads in Woolwich.

debate: Delegates and councillors spoke in favour of the full ION light rail extension to Cambridge. Arguments included accessibility for people with disabilities, long bus trips, and the case for permanent rail infrastructure over bus rapid transit.

Some councillors were frustrated that Stage 2 ION will take two to two and a half years to reach a full business case. Staff said the work and funding requests proceed in parallel and that land acquisition and design come first. Staff would not give a construction start or opening date.

On George Street North, some councillors opposed closing the land because the owner built on regional land and it could set a precedent. Staff said the owner would pay all costs and the appraised value, and that the owner would be required to remove the structures otherwise. Others saw it as recouping costs.

On right turn on red, one councillor said they could not support a general ban and wanted no blanket policy. The mover said it was a feasibility study for select intersections. Another councillor asked for collision data split by turn type.

On Highland Road, staff said a noise wall would cost about $8.56 million for roughly 100 homes and could expose the Region to wider claims. They pointed to roundabout treatments, tight fences and street design changes instead.
